userStories.title: Self-service password change
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add authenticated password change that preserves the caller's session and revokes the user's other active sessions.

**Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin.

**Approach** — Verbatim password-change design:

`POST /api/auth/password`, body `ChangePasswordDto { currentPassword: string; newPassword: string }`. `currentPassword` is `@IsString` + `@MinLength(1)`. `newPassword` uses the same validators as `RegisterDto.password` (`@IsString`, `@MinLength(8)`, `@Matches(PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY)`, same i18n messages). The route is authenticated (no `@Public()`), declares `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` + `@Requires('session.password.change')`, and is throttled with `@Throttle({ default: { limit: AUTH_LOGIN_LIMIT, ttl: AUTH_LOGIN_TTL_MS } })`.

`AuthService.changePassword(principal: KodaPrincipal, dto: ChangePasswordDto): Promise<void>`:
1. A principal that is not a user principal (`isUserPrincipal` false: an agent or runner), or a user principal without `sessionId` (an access token issued before sessions; none can still be valid, since access tokens live 15 minutes and sessions shipped in #460) → `AuthException({}, 'auth')` (401). Load the user with `authRepo.findUserById(principal.id)`; missing or `disabled` → `AuthException({}, 'auth')` (401).
2. `bcrypt.compare(dto.currentPassword, user.passwordHash)` false → `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'auth.currentPasswordWrong')` (403). A 403, not a 401, so the web's 401 refresh-and-retry does not run.
3. Hash the new password with `bcrypt.hash(dto.newPassword, 12)` before opening the transaction. Then, in one `audit.audited(...)` call (it opens the transaction): `authRepo.updatePasswordHash(user.id, hash)`, then `authSessions.revokeAllForUser(user.id, 'password-change', now, principal.sessionId)`. From US-003 on, the same transaction also deletes the user's unused `PasswordResetToken` rows (`PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId)`), so a reset link emailed before the change stops working. The audit entry is `{ key: 'session.password.change', resourceType: 'user', resourceId: user.id, projectId: null, summary: 'password changed' }`.
4. After the commit: for each revoked session id, `withAuthSessionCacheLock(id, () => cache.invalidate(authSessionCacheKey(id)))`; then `cache.invalidate(userAuthStateCacheKey(user.id))`.
5. The controller answers `JsonResponse.Ok({})` (200). The caller's session and cookies stay valid.

`AuthSessionService.revokeAllForUser(userId: string, reason: SessionRevokeReason, now: Date, exceptSessionId?: string): Promise<string[]>` revokes every active session of the user (`revokedAt: null`, `expiresAt > now`) except `exceptSessionId`, sets `revokedReason`, and answers the revoked ids. It runs no transaction of its own and records no audit entry: its caller runs it inside the audited transaction. It goes through a new repository method `PrismaAuthSessionRepository.revokeActiveSessionsOfUser(userId, reason, now, exceptSessionId?)` built on `updateManyAndReturn` (the same Prisma call `revokeSession` uses).

Catalog design: Three new keys, each added in four places: one REST row in the inventory TSV `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv` (next to the `session.*` rows, same columns), `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS` plus the access set in `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts`, the key lists in `catalog.spec.ts`, and one cell per role in `src/permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json`. For this story: `session.password.change`, `POST /auth/password`, TSV `own (see design §1)`, INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS `own`, access set `IMPLICIT_KEYS`, every role cell `["implicit","implicit"]`. Keep every other catalog assertion and snapshot cell unchanged. After the API contract changes, `bun run generate` from the repo root keeps `openapi.json` and the CLI client current.

API message design: The exception filter translates `<prefix>.<code>`, so both messages are nested under their exception codes in `apps/api/src/i18n/en/auth.json` and `zh/auth.json`, the way `invites.json` nests `roleGone`: `"currentPasswordWrong": { "40003": "The current password is incorrect" }` (`ForbiddenAppException`). Add the Chinese equivalent.

**Scope** — In: change route/DTO, password-hash repository update, bulk session revoke, atomic audit, cache eviction, permission inventory/catalog/snapshot and API translations/contracts. Out: reset storage/email (US-002), the PasswordResetTokenStore dependency and outstanding-link deletion until US-003, reset routes (US-003/004), recovery binding (US-005) and web forms (US-006/007). No password-history, same-password rejection or session-list UI.

**Interface** — `ChangePasswordDto { currentPassword: string; newPassword: string }`; `AuthService.changePassword(principal: KodaPrincipal, dto: ChangePasswordDto): Promise<void>`; `PrismaAuthRepository.updatePasswordHash(userId, passwordHash): Promise<void>`; `AuthSessionService.revokeAllForUser(userId: string, reason: SessionRevokeReason, now: Date, exceptSessionId?: string): Promise<string[]>`; `PrismaAuthSessionRepository.revokeActiveSessionsOfUser(userId, reason, now, exceptSessionId?)`.

Verification: Use existing auth service/controller tests and add real HTTP/persistence cases under test/integration/auth. Prime session activity caches before revocation assertions, use resetThrottle for throttle isolation and keep other users' sessions intact. Test the no-session principal at unit level; an agent HTTP case covers the shared non-user guard without a separate runner case.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] When POST /api/auth/password receives the caller's correct currentPassword and a valid newPassword, it answers 200, and a later POST /api/auth/login succeeds with newPassword and answers 401 with the old password.
AC-2 [integration] After that change, the caller's own access token still answers 200 on GET /api/auth/me, and its refresh token still rotates on POST /api/auth/refresh.

AC-3 [integration] After that change, a second session of the same user whose access token answered 200 on GET /api/auth/me before the change (so its activity is cached) is revoked with revokedReason password-change, and that access token answers 401 on GET /api/auth/me right after the change.
AC-4 [integration] After that change, a session of a different user stays active.
AC-5 [integration] When POST /api/auth/password receives a wrong currentPassword, it answers 403 with the auth.currentPasswordWrong message, the stored hash is unchanged, and no session is revoked.
AC-6 [integration] When currentPassword is wrong, no session.password.change audit entry is recorded.
AC-7 [integration] A successful change records exactly one audit entry { key: 'session.password.change', resourceType: 'user', resourceId: <userId>, projectId: null, summary: 'password changed' }.
AC-8 [integration] When POST /api/auth/password receives an agent API key, it answers 401 and writes nothing.
AC-9 [unit] AuthService.changePassword with a user principal that has no sessionId throws AuthException and calls neither updatePasswordHash nor revokeAllForUser.
AC-10 [integration] When newPassword is short1! (fewer than 8 characters), POST /api/auth/password answers 400 and the stored hash is unchanged.
AC-11 [integration] When newPassword lacks an uppercase letter (lowercase1!), POST /api/auth/password answers 400 and the stored hash is unchanged.
AC-12 [unit] AuthSessionService.revokeAllForUser('u1', 'password-change', now, 's1') answers the ids the repository's revokeActiveSessionsOfUser('u1', 'password-change', now, 's1') returned.
AC-13 [integration] PrismaAuthSessionRepository.revokeActiveSessionsOfUser leaves an already-revoked session's revokedReason and revokedAt unchanged and does not return its id.
AC-14 [unit] The catalog entry for session.password.change has access implicit.
AC-15 [integration] POST /api/auth/password is throttled like POST /api/auth/login: after AUTH_LOGIN_LIMIT requests from one client inside AUTH_LOGIN_TTL_MS, the next answers 429.

routing.reasoning: Password hashing, principal restrictions, audited multi-write transactions and immediate session-cache revocation cross multiple modules; security override requires strict test/implementation isolation.

suggestedCriteria: AuthService.changePassword throws AuthException without password or session writes when findUserById returns null or a disabled user.
revokeActiveSessionsOfUser does not change or return a session whose expiresAt equals now.
When the password-change audit write fails, the password hash and all session revocation fields retain their pre-change values.

userStories.title: Password reset store and email plumbing
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add durable one-time reset-token storage and non-retryable localized reset-email scheduling without exposing a route. **Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin. **Approach** — Verbatim reset-storage design: New model, migration `20261210100000_password_reset_tokens`: ```prisma model PasswordResetToken { id String @id @default(cuid()) userId String user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade) tokenHash String @unique // lowercase sha256 hex of the raw token expiresAt DateTime usedAt DateTime? createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @@index([userId]) } ``` `User` gains the back-relation `passwordResetTokens PasswordResetToken[]`. The raw token is `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')`, hashed with sha256 the way `generateInviteToken` / `hashInviteToken` (`apps/api/src/projects/invites/invite-token.ts`) do; only the hash is stored. `PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MS = 30 * 60_000`. A new module-private `PrismaPasswordResetRepository` (`apps/api/src/auth/password-reset/prisma-password-reset.repository.ts`) owns the table with four methods: `replaceUnused(userId, tokenHash, expiresAt): Promise` (deletes the user's unused rows and inserts the new one in one `txManager.run`), `findByHash(tokenHash): Promise<{ id; userId; expiresAt; usedAt; userDisabled } | null>`, `markUsed(id, now): Promise` (`updateMany where { id, usedAt: null }`, the affected count) and `deleteUnusedOf(userId): Promise`. `PasswordResetTokenStore` (below) is its only consumer and the public face of the table. No `@nathapp/nestjs-*` package covers password reset (plugin catalog checked 2026-11-15: the closest match, `nestjs-iam`, is roles and policies), so the flow is built here on the existing email schedule. `PasswordResetStoreModule` (`apps/api/src/auth/password-reset/password-reset-store.module.ts`, US-002) is a leaf: it imports only `PrismaModule`, provides `PrismaPasswordResetRepository` and `PasswordResetTokenStore`, and exports `PasswordResetTokenStore`. `PasswordResetTokenStore` (`password-reset-token.store.ts`) is the public face of the table: `replaceUnused`, `findByHash`, `markUsed` and `discardUnusedFor(userId): Promise`, each delegating to the repository. `PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId)` deletes the user's unused reset tokens and runs inside its caller's transaction; `AuthService.changePassword` calls it from US-003 on. Verbatim email plumbing: - `EmailKind` (`email-schedule.types.ts`) and `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_CODES` (`templates/template-codes.ts`) gain `PASSWORD_RESET`. - `EN_TEMPLATES` gains `PASSWORD_RESET`: subject `[koda] Reset your password`, html `

Someone asked to reset the password of your koda account.

Choose a new password

This link works once and expires on {{expiresAt}}. If you did not ask for it, ignore this email.

`. `ZH_TEMPLATES` gains the Chinese equivalent. - `EmailScheduleService.startPasswordResetSend(input: PasswordResetSend)` and `EmailScheduleRepository.startPasswordResetSend`, mirroring `startInviteSend` with `kind: 'PASSWORD_RESET'`, `userId` set and `inviteId` null. `PasswordResetSend = { userId: string; toEmail: string; locale: string; now: Date }`. - `EmailScheduleRepository.closeAbandonedInvites(now)` closes abandoned `PASSWORD_RESET` rows too: its `where.kind` becomes `{ in: ['INVITE', 'PASSWORD_RESET'] }`. `claimDue` already claims only `NOTIFICATION` and `MEMBER_ADDED`, so reset rows are never re-sent. - The `EmailSchedule.kind` schema comment lists `PASSWORD_RESET`. **Scope** — In: exact model/migration, leaf module/repository/store/constants, reset email kind/code/templates, schedule service/repository start operation and abandoned closing. Out: request/confirm controller/service and module wiring (US-003/004), change-password integration with the store (US-003), refresh-client columns (US-005), web pages (US-006/007), expired/used-row purge and email retries. **Interface** — `replaceUnused(userId, tokenHash, expiresAt): Promise`; `findByHash(tokenHash): Promise<{ id; userId; expiresAt; usedAt; userDisabled } | null>`; `markUsed(id, now): Promise`; repository `deleteUnusedOf(userId): Promise`; store `discardUnusedFor(userId): Promise`; `EmailScheduleService.startPasswordResetSend(input: PasswordResetSend)`; `PasswordResetSend = { userId: string; toEmail: string; locale: string; now: Date }`; `PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MS = 30 * 60_000`. Implementation note: The later request design requires two concurrent requests not to leave two unused rows. PostgreSQL transaction atomicity alone does not serialize delete/insert with an initially empty token set; use per-user serialization inside replaceUnused without changing its interface or specified schema. markUsed and discardUnusedFor must use the current transaction client rather than opening independent transactions. Verification: Add real Postgres store/schedule tests and a no-DB leaf-module compilation test. Extend existing email-schedule repository and template/seeder tests. The closeAbandonedInvites where-clause assertion becomes kind: { in: ['INVITE', 'PASSWORD_RESET'] }; the status and lock conditions stay. The seeder already loops codes and locales; new reset templates must be seeded for both en and zh without making reset rows eligible for dispatcher claiming.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] PasswordResetTokenStore.replaceUnused(userId, tokenHash, expiresAt) deletes the user's unused token rows and inserts the new one, so afterwards exactly one unused row exists for the user, carrying the given tokenHash and expiresAt.
AC-2 [integration] replaceUnused leaves a used row (usedAt set) of the same user in place.
AC-3 [integration] replaceUnused leaves another user's unused row in place.
AC-4 [integration] PasswordResetTokenStore.findByHash(tokenHash) answers { id, userId, expiresAt, usedAt, userDisabled } for a stored hash, or null for an unknown hash.
AC-5 [integration] PasswordResetTokenStore.markUsed(id, now) answers 1 for an unused row and 0 when the row already has usedAt.
AC-6 [unit] PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MS equals 1,800,000 (30 minutes).

AC-7 [integration] EmailScheduleService.startPasswordResetSend({ userId, toEmail, locale: 'en', now }) writes one EmailSchedule row with kind PASSWORD_RESET, status SENDING, the userId, inviteId null and lockedUntil two minutes after now.
AC-8 [unit] EmailScheduleRepository.closeAbandonedInvites marks a PASSWORD_RESET row in status SENDING with lockedUntil in the past as FAILED with lastError abandoned.
AC-9 [integration] EmailScheduleService.claimDue never returns a PASSWORD_RESET row, even one in status PENDING with dueAt in the past.
AC-10 [unit] EN_TEMPLATES.PASSWORD_RESET has the subject [koda] Reset your password and an html body containing the {{url}} and {{expiresAt}} placeholders.
AC-11 [unit] ZH_TEMPLATES.PASSWORD_RESET has a non-empty subject and an html body containing the {{url}} and {{expiresAt}} placeholders.
AC-12 [unit] The email template seeder seeds a PASSWORD_RESET template for both en and zh.
AC-13 [unit] Regression: Given an INVITE EmailSchedule row in SENDING with lockedUntil before now, EmailScheduleRepository.closeAbandonedInvites(now) still marks it FAILED with lastError abandoned.

routing.reasoning: New transactional token store, migration, module boundary and one-shot email integration are security-critical despite having no route yet.

suggestedCriteria: When two replaceUnused calls for the same user execute concurrently with no initial token rows, exactly one unused token remains after both calls finish.
PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId) deletes only that user's unused rows and returns their affected count, leaving used rows and other users' rows unchanged.
When an enclosing transaction rolls back after discardUnusedFor, the deleted unused tokens remain available.

the `PasswordResetToken` model, the `User.passwordResetTokens` back-relation and the `EmailSchedule.kind` comment.

userStories.title: Password reset request route
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a non-enumerating public reset-request endpoint with detached email work and invalidate outstanding reset links after password change.

**Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin.

**Approach** — Verbatim modules design:

Two modules, so `AuthModule` never imports `NotificationsModule` (that would close the cycle `AuthModule` → `NotificationsModule` → `LiveModule` → `AuthModule`; the repo avoids it the same way with `AuthRepositoryModule` and `AuthSessionsModule`):
- `PasswordResetStoreModule` (`apps/api/src/auth/password-reset/password-reset-store.module.ts`, US-002) is a leaf: it imports only `PrismaModule`, provides `PrismaPasswordResetRepository` and `PasswordResetTokenStore`, and exports `PasswordResetTokenStore`. `PasswordResetTokenStore` (`password-reset-token.store.ts`) is the public face of the table: `replaceUnused`, `findByHash`, `markUsed` and `discardUnusedFor(userId): Promise<number>`, each delegating to the repository.
- `PasswordResetModule` (`password-reset.module.ts`, US-003) declares `PasswordResetController`, provides `PasswordResetService`, and imports `PasswordResetStoreModule`, `AuthRepositoryModule` (`PrismaAuthRepository`), `AuthSessionsModule` (`AuthSessionService`) and `NotificationsModule` (`EmailDispatcher`); `EmailAvailability` and `EmailScheduleService` come from the global `EmailCoreModule`. `AppModule` imports `PasswordResetModule`.
- `AuthModule` imports `PasswordResetStoreModule` only, so `AuthService.changePassword` can call `PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor`.

Controller design: `PasswordResetController` (`apps/api/src/auth/password-reset/password-reset.controller.ts`, `@Controller('auth')`, `@ApiTags('auth')` like `AuthController`) hosts both reset routes: handler `requestReset` on `@Post('password-reset')` and handler `confirmReset` on `@Post('password-reset/confirm')`, each `@HttpCode(200)`. Both routes are public, so the controller carries no `@ApiBearerAuth` (an exception to `.nax/rules/api-controllers.md` for unauthenticated routes, like `register` and `login`). `AuthController` is unchanged by the reset routes. Story boundary: this story creates the controller with requestReset only; confirmReset is added by US-004.

Verbatim request design:

`POST /api/auth/password-reset`, body `PasswordResetRequestDto { email: string }` (`@IsEmail`, `@MaxLength(254)`, same messages as `RegisterDto.email`). The route is public (`@Public()`, `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('session.password.reset.request')`), throttled with `AUTH_LOGIN_LIMIT` / `AUTH_LOGIN_TTL_MS`, and always answers `JsonResponse.Ok({})` (200).

`PasswordResetService.request(email: string, locale: EmailLocale): Promise<void>` returns after the user lookup. When the user exists, is not disabled and `EmailAvailability.configured` is true, it starts a detached task (not awaited; a rejection is caught and logged with `Logger.warn`). The whole task runs inside `bookkeeping('auth.password-reset-request', ...)`, a new reason in `BOOKKEEPING_REASONS` (`apps/api/src/action-context/audit-coverage.reasons.ts`, sentence: "A password reset token and its email schedule row, written for a public request that records no audit entry so it cannot reveal whether the address has an account."), so its writes never count against the request's audit scope, whether they land before or after the handler completes. The task:
1. calls `PasswordResetTokenStore.replaceUnused(userId, sha256(raw), now + PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MS)`, which deletes the user's unused reset tokens and inserts the new one in one transaction, so two concurrent requests cannot leave two unused tokens;
2. calls `EmailScheduleService.startPasswordResetSend({ userId, toEmail, locale, now })`, which inserts a `PASSWORD_RESET` row in status `SENDING`;
3. sends it with `EmailDispatcher.sendOne(row, 'PASSWORD_RESET', { url: EmailAvailability.webUrl('/reset-password/<raw>'), expiresAt: <ISO> }, userId, now, false)`. Retry is off: only the hash is stored, so a failed send is final.

The controller resolves the locale from `Accept-Language` with a local helper that copies the rule of the module-private `inviteLocale` in `project-invites.controller.ts` (only a value starting with `zh` gives `zh`; anything else is `en`).

Token material follows the storage design: The raw token is `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')`, hashed with sha256 the way `generateInviteToken` / `hashInviteToken` (`apps/api/src/projects/invites/invite-token.ts`) do; only the hash is stored. `PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MS = 30 * 60_000`.

Password-change seam: `PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId)` deletes the user's unused reset tokens and runs inside its caller's transaction; `AuthService.changePassword` calls it from US-003 on. `AuthModule` imports the leaf `PasswordResetStoreModule` (never `PasswordResetModule`) from US-003 on; `AuthService` gains the constructor dependency `PasswordResetTokenStore`. The existing password-change audited work must include discardUnusedFor before commit so old reset links stop working.

Catalog: add `session.password.reset.request` as `POST /auth/password-reset`, scope `public`, access `PUBLIC_KEYS`, every role cell `["public","public"]`, in the inventory TSV, INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS/access set, catalog.spec.ts key lists and role-matrix.json. Place it next to session.refresh; keep unrelated assertions/cells unchanged. The TSV row is session/global. Regenerate openapi.json and CLI artifacts with root `bun run generate`. Add `auth.password-reset-request` to EXPECTED_REASON_IDS in audit-coverage.bookkeeping.spec.ts without changing its exact-list assertion or the seven unaudited surfaces. Add a PasswordResetTokenStore double to auth.service.spec.ts and session-activity-fence.spec.ts, preserving fence assertions and asserting discardUnusedFor occurs inside audited work.

**Scope** — In: request DTO/controller/service/module, detached bookkeeping-scoped token/email task, app wiring, permission contract and password-change token invalidation. Out: persistence/email primitives (US-002), confirm route/DTO/algorithm (US-004), client-bound refresh (US-005), web forms (US-006/007), equal lookup timing and per-email throttling. Log only user id and failure reason, never raw token or URL; no separate log-token-absence test is required.

**Interface** — `PasswordResetRequestDto { email: string }`; `PasswordResetService.request(email: string, locale: EmailLocale): Promise<void>`; controller `requestReset` on `@Post('password-reset')`; `PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId): Promise<number>`; `EmailDispatcher.sendOne(row, templateCode, data, userId, now, retryable = true): Promise<SendOutcome>`.

Verification: Write request HTTP integration cases with audit-coverage checking enabled, injected email collaborators and bounded polling up to 5 seconds for detached work. Unknown-address absence uses the same wait. Assert FAILED final state for channel failure, and both returned FAILED and rejected task failures must be warning-logged appropriately. Add no-DB module compilation coverage to expose circular or missing provider wiring.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] POST /api/auth/password-reset for an existing, enabled user with email configured answers 200 {}, and (the test polls up to 5 s for the detached task) a PasswordResetToken row appears for that user with expiresAt 30 minutes after the request and usedAt null.
AC-2 [integration] The stored tokenHash is the lowercase sha256 hex of the raw token in the emailed /reset-password/<raw> URL, and the raw token is stored in no column.

AC-3 [integration] The email is sent through EmailDispatcher.sendOne with template code PASSWORD_RESET, data.url equal to EmailAvailability.webUrl('/reset-password/<raw>'), and the sixth argument false (no retry).
AC-4 [integration] One EmailSchedule row of kind PASSWORD_RESET with the user's id is written and ends in status SENT when the send succeeds.
AC-5 [integration] When the email channel throws on send, the response is still 200 {}, the EmailSchedule row ends in status FAILED, and the failure is logged with Logger.warn.
AC-6 [integration] A request for an unknown address answers 200 {} and, after the same 5 s wait, no PasswordResetToken row and no EmailSchedule row exist for it, and no email is sent.
AC-7 [integration] A request for a disabled user answers 200 {}, writes no token row and sends no email.
AC-8 [integration] A request while email is not configured answers 200 {}, writes no token row and sends no email.

AC-9 [integration] A known and an unknown address both answer 200 with the same body, and neither raises UnauditedWriteError (the test runs with audit-coverage checking on, as the integration harness does).
AC-10 [integration] A second request for the same user leaves exactly one unused token row for that user.
AC-11 [integration] A request with Accept-Language: zh-CN writes the EmailSchedule row with locale zh; one with Accept-Language: fr writes en.
AC-12 [integration] POST /api/auth/password-reset is throttled like POST /api/auth/login: after AUTH_LOGIN_LIMIT requests from one client inside AUTH_LOGIN_TTL_MS, the next answers 429.
AC-13 [unit] The catalog entry for session.password.reset.request has access public.
AC-14 [integration] After a reset request, a successful POST /api/auth/password by that user deletes the outstanding unused reset token, so confirming it later answers 400.
AC-15 [integration] A body whose email is not an email address answers 400 and writes nothing.

routing.reasoning: The new reset module joins existing token-store, bookkeeping, audited-change and one-shot email patterns rather than introducing a new architecture; its public credential-recovery flow still requires the security-mandated strict TDD strategy.

suggestedCriteria: When the detached token-write task rejects, requestReset still answers 200 with the same envelope and Logger.warn records the failure.
When email delivery stays pending, PasswordResetService.request resolves without waiting for the send to finish.
When password-change audited work rolls back after discarding reset tokens, the previously unused reset token remains stored.

userStories.title: Password reset confirmation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Consume an emailed reset token exactly once, change the password and revoke every session without signing the user in.

**Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin.

**Approach** — Verbatim confirm design:

`POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm`, body `PasswordResetConfirmDto { token: string; newPassword: string }`, `token` `@IsString` + `@MinLength(1)` + `@MaxLength(128)`, `newPassword` validated like `RegisterDto.password`. Public (`@Requires('session.password.reset.confirm')`), throttled the same way.

`PasswordResetTokenStore.discardUnusedFor(userId)` deletes the user's unused reset tokens and runs inside its caller's transaction; `AuthService.changePassword` calls it from US-003 on.

`PasswordResetService.confirm(dto: PasswordResetConfirmDto, now: Date): Promise<void>`:
1. Hash the token and find the row with its user.
2. Missing, `usedAt` set, `expiresAt <= now`, or the user disabled → `ValidationAppException({}, 'auth.resetTokenInvalid')` (400).
3. Hash the new password before opening the transaction. In one `audit.audited(...)` call: mark the row used with `updateMany where { id, usedAt: null }` (count 0 → the same 400, thrown inside so the transaction rolls back), `updatePasswordHash`, `bumpTokenVersion`, `authSessions.revokeAllForUser(userId, 'password-reset', now)`, delete the user's other unused reset tokens. Audit entry `{ key: 'session.password.reset.confirm', resourceType: 'user', resourceId: userId, projectId: null, summary: 'password reset' }`.
4. After the commit: evict each revoked session's `authSessionCacheKey` under its lock, `cache.invalidate(userTokenVersionCacheTag(userId), { mode: 'tag' })` and `cache.invalidate(userAuthStateCacheKey(userId))`.
5. Answer `JsonResponse.Ok({})`. No session is issued; the web sends the user to `/login`.

userStories.title: Account password form and User-Agent forwarding
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide the account password-change form and forward the browser's User-Agent through Nuxt auth proxy calls.

**Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin.

**Approach** — Verbatim web forwarding design:

`forwardToApi` (`apps/web/server/utils/api.ts`) forwards the incoming request's `user-agent` header as `User-Agent` when present, so the SSR refresh middleware, `server/api/auth/refresh.post.ts` and `server/api/auth/logout.post.ts` all present the browser's User-Agent. `clientIpHeaders` and `proxyHeaders` are unchanged.

Verbatim account-page and layout design:
- **Account page** `apps/web/pages/settings/account.vue`: a vee-validate + zod form with current password, new password and confirm new password (confirm must equal new; new must be at least 8 characters). It submits through `usePasswordActions().changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword })` (`apps/web/composables/usePasswordActions.ts`), which calls `$api.post('/auth/password', ...)`. Success shows a `useAppToast()` success toast and resets the form. A 403 shows the `auth.account.currentPasswordWrong` message on the current-password field; any other error shows `extractApiError()`.
- **Layout:** the header in `apps/web/layouts/default.vue` gains an "Account" link (`data-testid="header-account-link"`) to `/settings/account`, next to the logout button.
- **i18n:** every new string is in both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`, under `auth.account`, `auth.forgot`, `auth.reset` and `nav.account`.
- The API calls go through the existing Nuxt catch-all proxy; none sets cookies, so no new Nitro route is needed.

For this story only auth.account and nav.account are introduced; US-007 adds auth.forgot/auth.reset. The integration bodies are exact: `POST /auth/password` with `{ currentPassword, newPassword }`. Do not submit confirmNewPassword to the API or manipulate auth cookies on success; US-001 preserves the caller's session. The UA forwarded here is the same one US-005 hashes on refresh, including SSR middleware requests, not the Nuxt runtime's own UA. When absent, send no User-Agent header.

**Scope** — In: account page, thin changePassword composable action, header link, en/zh strings and shared forwardToApi UA forwarding covering SSR/refresh/logout. Out: forgot/reset actions/pages/login and guest-route changes (US-007), API password mutation (US-001), API recovery algorithm (US-005), client-IP/proxy policy changes, session list and logout-all UI. Do not expand password policy beyond the specified frontend minimum/matching checks.

**Interface** — `usePasswordActions().changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword })`; `$api.post('/auth/password', { currentPassword, newPassword })`; existing `forwardToApi` signature stays unchanged and adds `User-Agent` when the incoming request has a `user-agent` header.

Repository integration notes: Read docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md before layout changes and update its Status/Decisions in the implementing PR. Keep inline navigation/source order and token-based styling; add the Account destination to CommandPalette per app guidance, without redesigning the shell. useApi converts HTTP FetchError envelopes into ApiError carrying the application ret; account 403 handling must recognize the real auth.currentPasswordWrong envelope code 40003 as well as raw HTTP status errors, rather than passing only mocked-status tests. Keep generic errors using extractApiError.

Verification: Extend forward-to-api.spec.ts and session-refresh.spec.ts to assert browser UA propagation and absence behavior. Existing forwardToApi assertions read individual keys, never the full header object, and layout specs do not pin the header button list. Add composable/form Jest tests for exact request body, mismatch prevention, success/reset, field 403 and generic failure; assert i18n parity. No new Nitro route is needed.

userStories.title: Forgot-password and reset-password pages
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the guest-facing email reset journey with non-enumerating request feedback, token confirmation and safe login routing.

**Motivation** — Users are admin-created with a temporary password, and a forgotten password needs an admin.

**Approach** — Verbatim web-page design:
- **Forgot password** `apps/web/pages/forgot-password.vue` (with `definePageMeta({ layout: 'auth' })`, as `login.vue` and `register.vue` do): an email form calling `usePasswordActions().requestReset(email)` (`$api.post('/auth/password-reset', { email })`); after the call settles it always shows the same "check your email" state.
- **Reset password** `apps/web/pages/reset-password/[token].vue` (layout `auth` too): new-password and confirm form calling `usePasswordActions().confirmReset(token, newPassword)` (`$api.post('/auth/password-reset/confirm', { token, newPassword })`). Success navigates to `/login?reset=1`; a 400 shows the "link invalid or expired" state with a link to `/forgot-password`.
- **Login page** `apps/web/pages/login.vue`: a "Forgot password?" link to `/forgot-password`, and a notice when the query has `reset=1`.
- **Routing:** `apps/web/middleware/auth.global.ts` treats `/forgot-password` and every path starting with `/reset-password/` as guest-only: anonymous visitors are not sent to `/login`, and authenticated users are redirected to `safeRedirectPath(to.query.redirect)`.
- **i18n:** every new string is in both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`, under `auth.account`, `auth.forgot`, `auth.reset` and `nav.account`.
- The API calls go through the existing Nuxt catch-all proxy; none sets cookies, so no new Nitro route is needed.

The reset form mirrors the upstream account form's vee-validate + zod new-password and confirm validation (new at least 8 characters; confirm equals new). auth.account and nav.account were added by US-006; this story adds auth.forgot and auth.reset, including the login reset notice/link text. Extend rather than replace usePasswordActions. Body contracts remain `{ email }` and `{ token, newPassword }` exactly. Reset success does not establish a session; navigating to login is intentional. Forgot feedback is identical even after rejection, including network or API failure.

**Scope** — In: forgot/reset auth-layout pages, composable requestReset/confirmReset actions, login link/reset notice, unified guest-only route predicate and en/zh strings. Out: account page/UA forwarding (US-006), request/confirm APIs (US-003/004), storage/email (US-002), reset for agents/runners, and automatic login or new Nitro cookie routes. Preserve existing login/register behavior, invite public-route exception and safeRedirectPath sanitization.

**Interface** — `usePasswordActions().requestReset(email)` → `$api.post('/auth/password-reset', { email })`; `usePasswordActions().confirmReset(token, newPassword)` → `$api.post('/auth/password-reset/confirm', { token, newPassword })`; `definePageMeta({ layout: 'auth' })`; success `navigateTo('/login?reset=1')`; authenticated guest-route redirect `safeRedirectPath(to.query.redirect)`.

Error seam: useApi can replace HTTP status errors with ApiError application codes. Ensure a genuine resetTokenInvalid response (-2 or 400 per the API exception contract) still enters the invalid/expired state; do not rely only on mocks carrying raw status=400. All user-facing copy must be localized.

Verification: Extend usePasswordActions and locale-parity tests created by US-006, login page tests and middleware tests. Existing middleware tests assert login/register behavior only and must remain true. Add page tests for resolved and rejected request feedback, route token propagation, confirm mismatch, success navigation and invalid-link recovery. Use the same guest-only predicate in both anonymous and authenticated branches so every /reset-password/ path gets consistent treatment; retain safe redirects for authenticated visitors.
